name: Austrian Arete
text: [overview] One to two pitches short of the summit area the arete flattens (4th class and some snow).
[detailed_rack] carry an axe and crampons for the descent.

name: Backside of Beyond
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.

name: Northeast Buttress
text: [overview] Descent is via the Banner-Ritter notch, then a glissade to Lake Catherine.
[overview] Reach the shoulder under the route over snow, starting from the Gem Lakes Trailhead past Thousand Island Lakes.
[approach] From camp, ascend the snowfield up to the shoulder under the climb and transition to the rock there;
[approach] an ice axe is needed on the snow, and crampons if it is frozen hard.
[descent_text] Head down toward the saddle separating Banner from Ritter, where both sides hold snow, so carry an ice axe.
[descent_text] From the saddle, glissade the snow slope below it back toward the lakes.

name: Barefoot Bynum
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.

name: Scavenger Hunt
text: [overview] Above the snowfield, around 100' up, sits a big roof shaped like a triangle.
[approach] Aim for the large triangular roof above the snowfield, which sits to the west of Treasure Hunt's first pitch.

name: Southwest Chimney
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — when coming in from the north side
[approach] Pass the cliffs and talus fields, then cross to the west side of the creek where it enters a canyon, and continue to Glacier Lake, where there are good bivy spots at the southwest corner.

name: Bloody Couloir
text: [overview] The ascent itself: snow reaching about 35 degrees lies under the couloir, which averages near 40 degrees.
[detailed_rack] Helmet, crampons and axe(s).
[what_to_bring] crampons.
[what_to_bring] ice axe or axes.
[approach] A broad snow apron rises from the lakes to the start of the couloir, which is split by a central pillar into a broader, less steep left chute and a narrower, steeper right chute.

name: Cascade Classic
text: [overview] Begin in the sloping gully and ascend it to the Australia snowfield.
[approach] This line begins in an angled gully, follows it to a broad snowfield, then takes the right-hand bowl into a left-hand gully that leads up to the summit ridge.

name: The McCramer
text: [overview] Begin at the left of the face and work across a horizontal snowfield to its right end.
[overview] From there, a simple mixed step leads up and to the right into a low-angle area of snow and rock.
[overview] Then go leftward across that ledge, ideally snow covered, and climb the initial gully encountered.
[overview] Past the gully's top, snow and then loose rock lead to the summit.

name: Dollar Couloir
text: [overview] Snow angle is about 35 degrees for most of it, reaching 41 degrees near 9,990ft.
[overview] Camping at the lake is possible, but avoid camping there when snow higher up is unstable.

name: Northeast Ridge
text: [description] From a high camp, follow the south side of the northeast ridge, crossing snow patches and then rock.

name: Kindergarten Gully
text: [detailed_rack] An ordinary ice screw rack, or a couple of pickets early in the season.

name: Dark Star
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.

name: Direct South Face
text: [descent_text] Beyond the saddle, sand or snow leads to the dirt road running along the creek's north bank, and you ford the creek at the point opposite your car.

name: East Buttress
text: [detailed_rack] Snow is likely on the approach and possibly the descent.

name: East Face - Ramp Route
text: [overview] Snow leads to the foot of the ramp.
[detailed_rack] Standard alpine rack, plus an ice axe depending on the season.

name: Eclipsed Arete
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.

[approach] Eclipsed Arete is the arete furthest left on the northeast face, beside Venusian Blind, and the approach is mostly the same: a snow chute and a traverse to the base of Venusian Blind, then a traverse left toward the arete.
[approach] Early-season snow may call for crampons.

name: North Couloir
text: [overview] Brief ice sections may appear, so crampons and an axe (or more) are recommended.

name: Land of Little Rain
text: [descent_text] From the saddle, sand or snow leads to the dirt road along the creek's north bank.

name: Antichrist Dihedral
text: [what_to_bring] crampons — may help if snow lies at the base
[approach] From the lake it is about an hour up to the Main Wall, a north-facing wall above the Lilliput Glacier.

name: West Chimney
text: [overview] Worth doing only when the pitch 2 chimney is full of snow.

name: East Couloir
text: [overview] Beneath the Matterhorn Glacier, the East Couloir is the higher of two ways onto the East Ridge.
[overview] Expect good snow in winter and a mixed scramble or scree slog by summer.
[approach] Where the trail climbs to a shallow col, leave it for a use trail up the ridge east of the glacier drainage to a small lake just under 10,000 feet, which has several campsites.

[approach] Continue up the moraine ridge to the toe of the Matterhorn Glacier, cross its short, nearly flat lower edge, and contour to the East Couloir, the higher of two ways onto the east ridge, in the gap on the left side of the peak.

[descent_text] The normal way down is the approach route: reverse the couloir (snow in winter and spring, loose scree and a mixed scramble by late summer), cross the glacier edge and drop the moraine ridge to the lake and the Horse Creek Trail.
[descent_text] Carry an axe and crampons while the couloir holds snow.

name: Mendenhall Couloir
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.
[approach] it holds steep snow low down and is typically climbed in late May or early June.

name: Moon Goddess Arete
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.
[approach] Leave the trail near Second Lake, where most parties camp, and cross to the foot of the crag by scree slopes or the snowfield.
[approach] A good option is a snow chute running up the wall that lies between the Sun Ribbon and Moon Goddess aretes;
[approach] crampons are useful early in the season.
[descent_text] Below the pass, snow or loose scree and talus lead back to the lakes.
[descent_text] Early in the season the snow below the pass can be kicked down or glissaded, but the scree and talus are loose and tiring.

name: Warning Shot (NW Face)
text: [what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — early season, for ice

name: Dana Couloir
text: [overview] Roughly 1,000 ft of 40-degree snow and ice, a friendly introduction to gully ice.
[what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — needed early in the season

name: Southeast Slopes from North Glacier Pass
text: [description] Walk to Thousand Island Lake and North Glacier Pass, then up easy slopes.

name: Southeast Ridge from Black Rock Pass
text: [description] Cross Glacier Pass and descend toward Cliff Creek, climb to Black Rock Pass, then traverse the ridge to the saddle at the base of the southeast ridge.

name: North Face
text: [overview] The first ascent stayed mostly on the rock walls, crossing between them to avoid snow and ice.
[overview] After heavy winters snow persists in the couloir into fall and turns to blue alpine ice at about 50 degrees.
[overview] If returning to Second Recess, take the Northwest ridge, also called the Glacier Route (class 2).
[detailed_rack] Bring screws and pickets for ice, plus some rock gear, chosen to suit conditions and your comfort.

name: Consolation Couloir
text: [detailed_rack] if wanted, pickets plus a few nuts.

name: North Face Couloir 1
text: [overview] An easy 2200 ft snow climb in the peaceful backcountry of the San Gabriels.
[overview] Avalanche danger is possible, as cornices and large avalanche-prone slopes sit near the top in winter.

name: North Face
text: [overview] The climb crosses the glacier to a clear couloir centered on the north face, ascends it (about 40 degrees) until a solid rock cap stops it, then veers right onto gentler terrain, mostly 3rd class, to reach the flat top before the summit itself.
[detailed_rack] Always: helmet, crampons and axe(s).
[approach] Descend a broad, low-angle scree chute, turn south and go up the recess, passing Snow Lakes, to reach the glacier under the north face.

name: Devil's Backbone
text: [detailed_rack] After or during heavy snowfall the ridge can hold cornices, deep drifts and ice, and a fall would be long.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — winter
[descent_text] When Harwood's snowfield blocks the ridge on the way up, the route skirts its lower southern edge to the saddle below Baldy's final slope.

[descent_text] In winter the ridge carries ice, deep drifts and cornices above long slopes on both sides, and it has caused fatal falls, so an axe and crampons and sound judgment about conditions are needed.

name: Harrington Couloir
text: [overview] Moderate snow and ice climb.
[detailed_rack] Conditions determine the mix of snow pickets, screws and rock protection that may prove handy.

name: North Face
text: [overview] Mostly 45 degree snow.

name: The Goode Life
text: [overview] Seasonal snow may need crampons or an axe later in the year.
[approach] Cross the moraine boulder fields to the second buttress left of the main buttress and go over a snowfield to the base.
[approach] Late in the season, ice may call for boots, crampons or an axe.

name: Avalanche Gulch
text: [overview] The standard and most-climbed route on Mount Shasta, a long snow climb gaining about 7,000 vertical feet from Bunny Flat to the 14,179 ft summit.
[overview] It is non-technical but steep and demanding, and needs an ice axe, crampons, a helmet and solid self-arrest skills.
[beta] From Helen Lake, climb straight up Avalanche Gulch on snow, heading between the dark rock of The Heart on the left and Thumb Rock on the right.
[beta] Most parties climb one of the steep snow or ice chutes that cut through the Red Banks;
[hazards] Steep snow and ice.
[obj_haz] Hard, icy snow in the morning where a slip can turn into a long slide.
[watch_out] Glissading with crampons on
[gear] Ice axe.
[gear] Crampons.
[detailed_rack] Gear needs run from none up through snow-climbing equipment and beyond, varying with the season and circumstances.
[what_to_bring] Glacier glasses and high-SPF sunscreen.
[what_to_bring] Extra layer or durable pants for glissading.
[what_to_bring] Stove and fuel for melting snow.
[what_to_bring] Ice axe.
